prompt:
Validate this Reformat transform. It should output read_epoch_ms, the milliseconds from the Unix epoch to read_at, together with meter_id and kwh.

Input port 0:
```xml
<Record name="MeterRead" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter="|" recordDelimiter="\n" nullValue="__NULL__">
  <Field name="meter_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="read_at" type="date" nullable="false" format="yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss" timeZone="UTC"/>
  <Field name="kwh" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
</Record>
```
Output port 0:
```xml
<Record name="MeterReadEpoch" type="delimited" fieldDelimiter="|" recordDelimiter="\n" nullValue="__NULL__">
  <Field name="meter_id" type="string" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="read_epoch_ms" type="long" nullable="false"/>
  <Field name="kwh" type="decimal" nullable="false"/>
</Record>
```

```ctl
//#CTL2
function integer transform() {
    date epoch = zeroDate;
    $out.0.meter_id = $in.0.meter_id;
    $out.0.read_epoch_ms = dateDiff($in.0.read_at, epoch, millisec);
    $out.0.kwh = $in.0.kwh;
    return ALL;
}
```

issues.text: The initializer is spelled `initgroup`, but Rollup requires `initGroup`. Case matters here: startup reports `Required function(s) initGroup() are missing!`, and the component cannot begin accumulating brix readings.

Even after correcting the initializer name, `a.score` has no assignment there. This nullable accumulator resets to null despite its metadata default of zero; the subsequent addition therefore lacks the required numeric baseline.

Nothing defines `updateGroup`, the required function that would consume each radio reading. Rollup rejects the transform during initialization, so neither the longest run nor its stability classification is calculated.

There is no `finishGroup` definition to approve the humidity summary for output. Once the separate field error is corrected, this omission still prevents Rollup initialization; no gallery counts can be processed.
`$out.0.damp` is not an output field; the supplied metadata calls it `wet`. This field-resolution error stops compilation before the missing-function check can report the absent lifecycle definition.

Before any cover measurement can contribute, Rollup needs `initGroup`, which this script omits. The missing initializer is a startup failure, rather than a group that happens to produce an empty vulnerability score.

Although `updateGroup` always returns false, `updateTransform` remains mandatory and has no definition here. Rollup lists it among the missing functions during initialization, alongside the absent initializer, and never starts the survey.
`a.weighted` is nullable and is used in addition without being initialized. Its reset value is null, so a numeric zero must be assigned explicitly before accumulating weighted cover.

The crossing counter is updated, but `finishGroup` is missing from the script. This required callback cannot be inferred from the state machine: Rollup fails initialization before it reads the first reservoir level.

A completed crossing count also needs `transform`, and no such function is declared. Its absence is another required-function initialization error; the existing `updateTransform` only disables per-record output and cannot emit a basin summary.

`initGroup` has not been provided to establish the excess sum and qualifying count. After fixing the undefined output field, Rollup will still reject initialization because this mandatory function is missing.

The guarded average has no `updateGroup` implementation supplying its operands. That missing mandatory function is independently fatal to initialization, even though the compiler first encounters the unrelated output-field error in this candidate.

The output schema declares `average_excess`, whereas the code writes `$out.0.mean_excess`. This invalid field reference fails compilation; the server cannot reach its missing-function checks until the mapping is repaired.

Only completion and per-record-output callbacks are present; `initGroup` is missing. Rollup therefore cannot initialize the transform, so even the first shipment never reaches the stage of counting a breach streak.

There is no `updateGroup` to extend an above-eight streak or break it on a missing temperature. Because that function is mandatory, Rollup reports an initialization failure instead of evaluating any temperature records.

The script also lacks `transform`, which must write the longest breach to the summary. Returning true from `finishGroup` does not replace this required function; its omission is detected before source rows are processed.

issues.text: No `initGroup` is declared for the salinity total and qualifying count. Both fields are non-nullable, but their reset behavior does not make the required initializer optional: Rollup rejects the script at startup.

`finishGroup` must be defined even when the only decision is to emit every estuary. This candidate omits it, which causes a required-function initialization error rather than merely suppressing groups without valid samples.

The per-record emitter `updateTransform` has been left out because accumulation returns false. Rollup nevertheless requires that definition at initialization; this transform cannot start processing samples until the callback is supplied.

`a.valid` counts only known, nonnegative samples. A group containing exclusively null or negative readings leaves it zero, so the current mean expression risks division by zero instead of returning the requested null.

The balance writer has no corresponding `initGroup` definition to start each precinct-round accumulator. Once the output-field typo is fixed, the missing required initializer still makes Rollup fail before processing any correction.

Signed deltas are never accumulated because `updateGroup` has no definition here. This is a missing mandatory callback, so Rollup initialization fails after the separate compile error is repaired; a zero balance is not produced.

No `updateTransform` function appears in this candidate, although Rollup requires it even for summary-only output. The absent callback is an initialization blocker independent of the output-field error and the other missing definitions.

`$out.0.net_ballots` refers to an undeclared field. The output record supplies `balance`, so compilation fails on field resolution before Rollup can perform the initialization check for missing functions.

`a.dose` is a nullable integer accumulator with an omitted additive initialization. Rollup resets it to null for each group even though its metadata contains a zero default, so arithmetic cannot assume zero.

`initGroup` is missing, so the Rollup stops at initialization rather than counting consents. Its required-function diagnostic names this callback; neither the consensus row nor the missing-evidence row can be produced.
The nullable `yes` accumulator resets to null, not zero. Once initialization is repaired, a positive consent reaches `a.yes + 1` and throws unless the initializer supplies the count baseline.

There is no `updateGroup` to consume a scan. This omission fails the component initialization check, before normalization or duplicate suppression can build a route; the existing output function cannot compensate for it.

`finishGroup` has not been implemented. Rollup rejects the transform during initialization because this mandatory callback is absent, so campaigns never reach the two endpoint rows already described by `transform`.
The `if (true)` block admits null observations into ordered date comparisons. A null arriving after a real endpoint can fail at runtime instead of being ignored as the specification requires.

The uppercase `Transform` is a different function from the required lowercase `transform`. The server reports `Required function(s) transform() are missing!` during initialization, before cue priorities or recognized-status counts are evaluated.

`updateGroup` is absent from the date-journal implementation. Initialization fails on that required callback, so no observation receives a start, backward, repeat, daily, or gap mark, regardless of the available helpers.

The journal also lacks `finishGroup`. Rollup requires that function before it accepts the transform, so the component cannot start and never reaches the existing cadence classification or summary output.

No `transform` callback writes the quorum summary. Its absence is caught during Rollup initialization, before checks are counted; neither a numeric agreement nor the required null result can be emitted.

`updateTransform` is missing as well. Returning false from `updateGroup` avoids per-record emission at execution time, but does not waive this definition; the component still fails initialization for the absent callback.
`finishGroup` returns false for an all-null group because its known count stays zero. After the callbacks are restored, that group would disappear instead of producing the requested null agreement.

The frost-spell code omits `initGroup`. Even though both non-nullable counters already have zero reset values, Rollup still requires this function and fails initialization before examining any frozen flag.
A `transform` definition is also needed to export the longest run. Rollup rejects this missing callback at startup; the otherwise usable run-tracking logic cannot execute or write a cabinet result.
`updateGroup` has been left out, so approval counting cannot even begin: Rollup rejects the component during initialization for this missing function, before it reads any cast or session records.
The approval fraction has no `transform` implementation. That absent mandatory output callback is a startup error, so the component cannot run far enough to compute or emit a session summary.

`updateTransform` must be supplied even when no per-record output is wanted. It is missing here, causing an initialization failure before the false-returning group-completion callback or any fraction calculation could matter.

The supplied `finishGroup` always returns false. Once the missing functions are added, this still suppresses every session summary, including sessions where all records were approved and the required fraction is one.
